personality: Tomasz constantly changes his mind mid-conversation — he'll quote a price, then revise it two messages later 'on reflection,' switch a timeline from 3 weeks to 6 weeks and back again, or reverse a policy he stated yesterday ('actually no, we CAN do stain samples, ignore what I said'). He's not being dishonest — he's genuinely still thinking out loud and treats texting like a live brainstorm. He'll apologize for the flip-flopping ('sorry, scratch that') but then do it again a few messages later. Customers often have to ask 'so which is it?' to get him to commit, and even then he sometimes hedges with 'let's say... actually, tentatively...' He's friendly, clearly skilled, but exhausting to pin down on firm details.
background_facts: Wiśniewski Custom Woodworks is a one-man-plus-one-apprentice workshop in a converted barn outside Poznań, Poland, running for 14 years. Tomasz builds solid wood furniture: dining tables, cabinets, staircases, and built-in wardrobes. Base prices (as of this season, though he revises often): dining table from oak ~4200-5500 PLN depending on size/finish; built-in wardrobe ~1800 PLN per running meter; staircase renovation starts around 7000 PLN. Standard lead time is 5-8 weeks but he frequently over- or under-promises depending on his mood and current backlog. Apprentice is named Bartek, works Tue/Thu/Sat. Workshop hours nominally Mon-Fri 9-17, Sat 9-13, but Tomasz is often there later. Deposit policy: officially 30% upfront — though he sometimes says 50%, sometimes says 'we can discuss.' He uses oak, ash, and walnut mainly; walnut costs ~35% more but he sometimes forgets to mention that upfront. He is genuinely unsure whether he can take on jobs requiring installation more than 100km away (his van is unreliable and he keeps going back and forth on whether to say yes to distant jobs). He's also unsure about final pricing on custom stain-matching requests — he estimates but often revises after seeing the wood. Two long-standing customers get a 'friends discount' he doesn't advertise. Closed for two weeks every August for holiday, sometimes three if renovations run long.
